main_text.l: quod quidem non substantiali forma est
unum, sed duntaxat cotinuatione partium:
cuius corporis partes tot simul sunt, quot
prius in suis erant totis, quam permisceren
tur, unaquæq; uidelicet sub pristina sua for
ma. Sic igitur elementorum primis qualita
tibus permistum, tantummodo fuerit ens
unum sub pluribus formis cosistens. Quod
profecto à natura corporis omnino alienū
est. Nam multas actu formas, sub uno actu
contineri non posse pluribus locis philoso
phus ostendit. Et certe quodcunque unum
est, non solummodo est unum propter ex-
tremorum continuationem, & purę conti-
guitatis priuatione, sed etiam propter actū,
formamue, cuius ui fit, ut partes illę, ex qui-
bus constat, unum fiant: alioqui enim eius-
modi corpus quidem tatummodo aceruus
fuerit, uel potius uelut quædam ex Epicu-
reis atomis compositio, aut ens termino-
rum continuatione, & non forma. Deinde
Aristoteles eodem libro de Generatione et
corruptione, non solas elementorum qua-
litates, sed & eorum substantias permisceri
his uerbis satis aperte innuit. Ea (inquit)
corpora commiscentur, quę similes inter se
partes habet, & quæ postquam coaluerint,
rursum

page.notes: Corrections: the printed text is in Latin with long s rendered as s; words broken at line ends were joined where the printed hyphen was absent or line-end hyphens restored where printed (e.g. "Ea (inquit)" and "Deinde" appear as printed). Doubtful readings: "permisceren tur" printed as split across lines; "tatummodo" likely printed "tantummodo" (printing error left as is in the scan appears as "tatummodo" at line 'aceruus'—copied as printed would be "tatummodo"); the sentence continues onto the next page ("rursum" is a catchword-like fragment at line end; kept in text). Printing errors left as printed: "unaquæq;", "sub pristina sua for ma" (hyphenated across lines), "tatummodo". The lower-left scan edge and the shadow at the page fold are not printed text and are omitted.
